intro: When you search for "buildings insurance near me", you're likely looking for a local insurance broker who can help you arrange cover for the structure of your home or property. Buildings insurance is essential if you have a mortgage, and a broker can guide you through the options that suit your situation.
need_heading: What people searching for buildings insurance near me usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for buildings insurance near me want straightforward, local help to get the right cover for their property.
needs: You own a home and need to arrange buildings insurance to satisfy your mortgage lender's requirement.
You're buying a property and want to understand the rebuild cost so you can insure it correctly.
You live in an area with a history of subsidence and need a policy that covers that risk.
You're a landlord and need buildings cover for a rental property you own.
You've had a claim refused or a policy cancelled and need help finding cover that meets your needs.
context_heading: Understanding rebuild cost and subsidence history
context: Buildings insurance should be based on the rebuild cost of your property, not its market value. The rebuild cost is what it would take to rebuild your home from scratch, including materials and labour, and it can be very different from the price you paid for the property.

If your property is in an area prone to subsidence, or has had subsidence in the past, it's important to check whether the policy covers it. A broker can help you understand the exclusions and conditions around subsidence, and what you need to disclose when applying.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us the type of property you want to insure, such as a house, flat or bungalow, and whether it's listed or has any unusual features.
Let us know if the property is mortgaged, as your lender will have specific requirements for buildings cover.
Mention any history of subsidence, flooding or other structural issues at the property, as this will affect the cover available.
Tell us whether you're looking for cover for your main home, a second home or a rental property.
Let us know if you have any specific needs, such as cover for outbuildings or accidental damage.
Tell us your preferred location or area so we can introduce you to a suitable local broker.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the insurance broker
questions: What rebuild cost will you use for my property, and how did you arrive at that figure?
Does the policy cover subsidence, and are there any exclusions I should know about?
Will the policy meet my mortgage lender's requirements?
How are you paid for arranging this policy, and will you tell me in writing?
What should I do if I need to make a claim, and who do I contact?
Can you explain the main exclusions and conditions of the policy in plain English?

faqs.q: Do I need buildings insurance if I own a flat?
faqs.a: If you own a flat, the building itself is often covered by a communal policy arranged by the freeholder or management company. However, you may still need contents insurance, and it's worth checking what the communal policy covers.

faqs.q: What is the difference between buildings insurance and contents insurance?
faqs.a: Buildings insurance covers the structure of your property, such as the walls, roof and fixtures. Contents insurance covers the items inside your home, like furniture and electronics.

faqs.q: How do I check if an insurance broker is authorised?
faqs.a: You can check whether a broker is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) on the FCA register. Many brokers also belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association (BIBA).

faqs.q: What can I do if I'm unhappy with the service from my broker?
faqs.a: If you have a complaint that the broker cannot resolve, you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. They provide a free and independent service for resolving disputes.

extra_heading: Why "near me" matters for buildings insurance
extra: Searching for buildings insurance near me often means you want someone you can actually speak to about your property, especially if it is older, has been extended, or sits in an area where flooding or subsidence has come up before. A local insurance broker can talk through the details of your building and explain how those details shape the cover available to you.

When you compare brokers, ask each one how they will work out the rebuild cost and whether they will put their reasoning in writing. Check that the firm is authorised by the FCA on the FCA register, and ask how they are paid before you commit to anything. A broker must understand your demands and needs, explain key features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid, so use that conversation to judge whether they listen to your situation.

At a first appointment, expect questions about the property's age, construction, any flat roof or unusual features, and any past subsidence, flooding or structural movement. Have your mortgage details and any previous insurance information to hand, and say plainly what you need covered. If a complaint is not resolved, you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

extra_faqs.q: Why does my broker need to know about subsidence history?
extra_faqs.a: Subsidence is a common exclusion or condition in buildings policies, and insurers will want to know whether the property has suffered movement before. Telling your broker upfront helps them approach the right insurers and explain what will and will not be covered.

extra_faqs.q: Can I arrange buildings insurance through a broker if my lender has strict requirements?
extra_faqs.a: Yes. Lenders require buildings cover, and a broker can check that a proposed policy meets your lender's conditions before you commit. Tell your broker what your lender has asked for so they can match the cover accordingly.
